decisions.reason: NL2's sentence 'If the signal transmission fails, it proceeds to the operational state' is narratively placed right after the InitialState->BrakingState clause, and the contract's own binding_hints fix source=BrakingState, target=OperationalState. The exact closed-model inventory (transition:line:12-19) and the complete source transition set (tr_0001-tr_0008) contain no BrakingState->OperationalState edge; the only Signal_Transmission_Fails edge (tr_0003 / transition:line:14) runs InitialState->OperationalState, and BrakingState's only outgoing edges go to ClampingState and InitialState. The S2 predicate ran on the exact bound endpoints and returned verdict=false with an explicit counterexample confirming the absence. This establishes the violation on the bound reading. A second competent reading remains available on these same facts: NL2 places the sentence directly after describing the InitialState->BrakingState transition, so 'it' could refer to the device generally rather than specifically to BrakingState, in which case the existing InitialState->OperationalState edge (transition:line:14) would satisfy the intended relation and BrakingState would be a misattributed source. Because both readings are compatible with the same closed inventory and the alternative is not defeated by an exact exclusionary NL clause (the binding_hints preference is itself an interpretive choice, not an explicit textual exclusion of the alternative referent), this alternative survives as an undercutting defeater rather than being defeated outright.
decisions.strongest_defeater: NL2 places the failure clause directly after describing the InitialState->BrakingState transition, so 'it' could refer to the device generally (just having been in InitialState) rather than specifically BrakingState; under that reading the existing InitialState->OperationalState edge (transition:line:14, Signal_Transmission_Fails) would satisfy the intended relation, making BrakingState a misattributed source rather than a genuinely missing edge.

stage_receipts.reason: Contracts extracted atomically: NL1 is context (describes overall device role, no independently violable obligation). NL2 yields an initial_entry (system/device begins at initial state, entering braking state on brake signal is modeled as endpoint since 'initial state' is itself a named operating state, not a pseudostate-owner distinction beyond the model's own Initial->Braking edge), plus three transition endpoints (Initial->Braking on brake signal; Braking->Operational on signal transmission failure; Operational->Initial on signal feedback sent) preserved together in one transition_groups row keyed by shared source only where applicable — since sources differ (Initial, Braking, Operational) across the narrative, I emit them as sequential group entries reflecting the narrated chain, plus separate endpoint contracts. NL3 yields a containment/transition-endpoint continuation: after entering Braking, system transitions to BrakeCaliperClamping, establishing Braking->BrakeCaliperClamping endpoint and implicit containment is not explicit here so no containment contract is manufactured (NL3 does not state BrakeCaliperClamping is a child of Braking, only that transition occurs to it after entering Braking, so only endpoint recorded). No cardinality, guard, or action obligations are explicitly stated beyond the transition triggers (brake signal, signal transmission failure, signal feedback sent), which are preserved as trigger/event on the group alternatives, not as standalone guard contracts since no separate data predicate is stated beyond the causing event/condition itself.
